name: CR-Diff-02-linearity-5.b
questiontext: Use the laws of logarithms to find the following derivative: \[ \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}} \left[{{CT:1}}\right]. \] [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: Using the laws of logarithms alg_logarithms we get \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \ln(1) - \ln({{CT:2}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle -\ln({{CT:3}}) - \ln({{CT:4}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}}{{CT:6}} - \ln({{CT:4}}) \end{array}\] So, by linearity calc_diff_linearity_rule, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:5}}{{CT:6}} - \ln({{CT:4}})\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:5}}{{CT:6}}\right] + \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[-\ln({{CT:4}})\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}}\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:6}}\right] + 0 \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}}{{CT:7}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:8}} \end{array}\]
